Quick-start guide
Use this guide online or open the downloaded copy offline. All screenshots are included. Website and RF links need internet access. Open the detailed setup guide.

Lights on Sunset Template Customiser

Make your Remote Falcon page your own.

Choose Lights on Sunset or Compact console, explore a seasonal style and personalise it for your show. No coding required. Each ready-made download includes all six seasonal starters and instructions.

By christmasdave · Lights on Sunset. The customiser personalises supplied layouts; each template retains its own visual identity.

Open the template customiser · Download Lights on Sunset · Download Compact console · Full setup guide

New to Remote Falcon? Remote Falcon lets visitors request or vote for songs at your light show. Use this customiser to personalise the page they see. Visit the official documentation to learn how to set up and connect your show.

Your current design sits beside the introduction on wider screens, with Change template close at hand. On smaller screens these stack above the settings. Restoring a saved theme shows a brief confirmation without moving the working area.

Lights on Sunset offers three logo designs per theme, including pixel-light displays, with an optional editable name heading. Choose Default, Rounded, Elegant, Festive or Spooky for the Home name, with an optional separate colour. A live sample shows your own name in the selected font, including in the wizard. A Home-name switch supports uploaded logos with lettering. Seven navbar decorations are available across Christmas and Halloween. Menu labels can be hidden for icons-only navigation, and the On air dot has an optional gentle glow. The header’s What’s new button separates Released updates from In progress summaries and planned themes. The newest release starts expanded with a green Latest badge; older releases start collapsed, and every release can be expanded or collapsed. Update HTML marks groups with viewer changes that require exporting your saved design again and replacing the installed RF HTML. Customiser-only changes need no export.

Choose a template, then a theme. One sample preview updates to match your choices; select Explore full preview for a centred phone view. Set up my show and Straight to editor stay in the footer while you browse. Setup asks for show details once. Finish with Apply & open editor. Tick Take a quick tour after setup for a short introduction to the shared editor; it starts unchecked each time setup opens. Existing saved designs resume in the editor.

Under Music → Player & queue, optionally show the maximum queue length above the song choices. RF supplies the value; 0 means unlimited. The local preview uses an illustrative limit of 10.

Choose navigation icons under Site setup → Navigation menu, message icons under Request messages, and other icons beside the feature they belong to. The Font Awesome 6.6 Free library is grouped into Christmas, Halloween, Harvest & summer, Lights & magic, Music & media, Social links and General. Search within a group or browse All. Playlist, resource and category-artwork choices use the same picker. Leaving Template default selected preserves the original icons.

Choose a template

The customiser now offers Lights on Sunset and Compact console. Use Change template to compare seasonal previews. Existing designs resume automatically. Choose Christmas, Halloween, Thanksgiving, Australia Day, US Patriotic or Valentine’s Day in either layout. Both templates keep a separate saved design for each theme.

Use Have an idea? in the chooser header to suggest a theme, share a viewer page or find the private-contact link. The GitHub viewer-submission form asks you to confirm that you have permission to share and adapt the page.

Undo / Redo works across templates, with separate history for each design during the current session. Typing in a text field keeps native text undo. Reloading clears editor history, but keeps saved settings. Reuse details from another saved design…, under Site setup → Theme & style or Change template, copies chosen details from another design saved in this browser. It does not import your existing RF viewer page.

Use the small Clear button below a text field to empty it. Editor changes can be restored with Undo; setup changes stay in the draft until you apply them. Required fields still need a valid value before export.

Compact console places music first, with Info and optional Support views. Its seasonal decorations, gentle motion, colour presets and date tiles can be adjusted in Site setup. Edit the small line above the show name under Music → Welcome → Tagline, or leave it blank to hide it. All saved themes for the selected template are included in its settings backup; only the selected theme is exported as RF HTML.

Get started in six steps

1. Add your show details

Choose Set up my show on the template selection screen for a short wizard: Your show, Dates & hours, Music & listening, Visitor guidance, then Review & finish. Using the season already selected, enter your name and optional logo, add show hours and choose FM, PulseMesh or both. Choose album artwork, category icons or no artwork for song lists, and control Now Playing artwork separately. Set individual category icons in Music after setup. In Visitor guidance, edit your neighbour-friendly message and choose whether and where it appears on the main screen while on air. Compact console also uses this message on Info. Back keeps your answers; Skip keeps the settings from when you entered that step, and Cancel discards setup changes. Everything remains editable afterwards.

Choose Straight to editor to skip setup. On the final review step, optionally tick Take a quick tour after setup before applying. Returning users resume their saved design directly.

Reopen Set up this design from the header at any time. The wizard shows the current template and season, starts with your current settings, and only saves when you choose Apply & open editor. Back keeps your answers; Skip keeps that step’s previous settings; Cancel changes nothing. Website dates and listening text do not change FPP or activate PulseMesh.

Open Help for this illustrated Quick-start guide, Take a quick tour, or Detailed setup help. The tour returns you to where you started without changing your settings. The downloaded quick-start guide works offline, with screenshots included.

2. Personalise the pages

AreaWhat you can change
Home (Lights on Sunset)Welcome, visitor guidance, announcements, extra information, off-air video and countdown
MusicSong artwork, Now Playing artwork, NEW sashes, Moving spotlights badges, categories, queue wording and counters. Compact console also keeps its welcome, announcement, off-air video and countdown here. Its visitor guidance is under Info.
SupportCards for charities, creators and thank-yous, with optional images and main-screen/Info links
InfoIntroduction, Quick Facts, FAQs, resources and a shortcut to social links and the separate YouTube button. Compact console also keeps extra-information cards and playlists here; Lights on Sunset’s playlists are edited under Music.
Site setupShow identity, dates, listening, colours, menu and optional social links
Request messagesRequest and voting titles and short explanations, with local preview buttons

Under Music → Song appearance, choose Category icons to replace song covers with an icon for each category. Use the shared picker for trees, snowmen, ghosts or other icons; choose Songs without a category for the fallback icon. Its default is a music note, as is any category without a chosen icon. Match category names and order to RF under Categories. Icons work even with filter buttons hidden. Show album artwork in Now Playing is independent; No artwork makes the song list text-only. Two artist-name switches independently control the song list and Now Playing / Up Next / queue. Both start on; missing artists leave no blank artist line.

Edit a viewer page contains the page buttons; selecting one opens its preview. General settings contains Site setup and Request messages, which keep the current preview page. Music is the starting page in Compact console.

Under Site setup → Theme & style, choose the season, colours and seasonal decorations. Theme buttons use a compact two-column layout, with the selected theme’s description underneath. Show dates & hours also holds Lights on Sunset’s optional on-air schedule switch. Listening holds FM, PulseMesh and the Music reminder option. Navigation menu brings menu labels, icons and Support visibility together.

On Music, Song selection holds request/voting headings and unavailable-song wording; Player & queue holds now-playing and queue wording, queue limits and counters; Off-air content holds the closed-show message and optional About link. Edit “All” under Categories, and “New this year” beside its switch in Song badges. Optional extras can stay off.

To hide Support from the visitor menu, untick Site setup → Navigation menu → Show Support in menu. Your Support page and saved content remain available, including through existing direct links. Support teasers on the main screen and Info still open their recipient links. Choose those placements for any cards visitors should find without the Support menu button.

For PulseMesh, choose Download app only, Listen on PulseMesh only or Both buttons under Site setup → Listening, or in the wizard. Listen needs your full public display link from PulseMesh. It is reused on the main screen (Home in Lights on Sunset, Music in Compact console) and in the listening FAQ. PulseMesh explains display links and supported plans; the buttons do not activate the service or change its access rules.

Extra cards and visitor guidance

Extra information supports up to five cards, each with a heading, message, optional image and optional link. Expand a card to edit it, reorder it or remove it. Find these cards on Home for Lights on Sunset and Info for Compact console.

Editor sections start collapsed. Open the section you need; changing pages keeps your manual open or closed choices. Explicit shortcuts and error links still reveal their target. In Lights on Sunset, Music link on Home has its own section under Home, separate from Welcome. Compact console does not have this Home shortcut.

Welcome can stay as plain text or use a card matching visitor guidance. Choose With show name, Above the header, Below the header or Below On air independently of the guidance position. Welcome stays visible on and off air with the show name, above or below the header; Below On air appears only while on air. When both messages share a position, welcome comes first. Turning welcome off keeps its wording, style and position for later. Existing and new designs keep welcome visible by default. With show name keeps the welcome close to the name. Existing saved positions, wording, style and visibility are preserved. These controls are shared by the editor and Quick Setup.

For Card like visitor guidance, turn on Use custom card colours to choose a Welcome-only background and text colour. These choices override the active theme and palette, without changing Visitor guidance. Use theme colours restores the theme styling and keeps your picked colours for later. Plain text ignores card colours. A contrast hint helps you choose readable text. Each saved design keeps its own choices.

Visitor guidance can appear above the header, below the header or below On air. Main-screen guidance appears only while on air. Compact console also keeps the same message on Info, including off air. Both templates keep guidance within each saved theme; use Reuse details from another saved design to copy it when needed.

Site setup → Header, logo & show name separates two choices, also available in setup:

- Header artwork changes the top image: keep the theme default, choose one of three included pictures, or choose No header artwork. - Logo sits below it: choose a simple icon, an included picture, your own HTTPS image, or No logo. Both templates support these choices.

You can show a chosen header with your own logo, or use an included picture as the logo and hide the top artwork. Show name, welcome text and lower decorations remain independent. Existing saved designs retain their appearance; reuse offers header and logo changes separately. Included styles use the destination theme’s pictures, shown in the reuse review. Setup choices are saved only when you apply setup.

Social links

Under Site setup → Social links, add up to eight links with an icon and visible label, then arrange their order. Show them on the main screen, Info or both. The main screen is Home in Lights on Sunset and Music in Compact console. Heading and message are optional. Links open in a new tab; this section starts off and retains your entries when hidden. Facebook, Instagram, YouTube and TikTok icons are in Social links in the shared picker. Expand Separate YouTube button on Info here to edit the optional labelled button below the Info introduction; it remains independent of the social row and the Off-air video card.

3. Check the preview

Try Mobile, Tablet or Desktop, then On air / Off air and Jukebox / Voting. The viewport choices check layout, not a particular phone's operating system. Mouse dragging scrolls phone/tablet previews; the wheel also works.

Reset demo clears sample requests, votes and feedback. Reset to defaults, in the settings controls, lets you reset This design or All saved designs across both templates. Each design uses its own theme defaults; imported song lists stay available. All-design reset also clears reuse-update links. You can Undo or Redo within each changed design during the current session. Back up each template first to keep a permanent copy. Neither reset changes an installed RF page.

The preview is a labelled demonstration with no connection to your show. Trying songs or messages does not send requests or votes to RF. Its mode switches are preview-only; RF controls the real viewer.

4. Bring your song list (optional)

In RF’s Sequences page, choose Export at the top to download your CSV. How to export from RF, beside the catalogue controls and under Music → Song badges, opens a short reminder with links to RF.

Use Import RF song CSV to choose a file and review its songs before importing. Under Choose song badges, mark each song as NEW, Moving heads, both or neither. All songs are imported, whether marked or not. Select Import & apply choices when ready; Cancel import, the X or Escape keeps your previous catalogue and settings. Detect categories sets up filter buttons so visitors can browse groups of songs. Category rows select RF categories by position: row 1 selects RF’s first category, row 2 its second, and so on. Renaming a button does not change its songs. Match RF’s names and order; this does not change categories saved in RF. Set song badges reopens both choices without typing exact sequence names. Manual entry is also available under Music → Song badges. Keep every category row in RF order and untick Show button for any filter you do not want; its songs stay under All. Songs without a category also appear under All (and New this year when marked NEW), but not under named category filters. They do not need an extra category row.

How category filters work opens a short guide from the import window or Music → Categories, with a link to RF’s category documentation. Import review counts songs without a category and recommends assigning every song one; you can still import and review them.

Your CSV stays in this browser. The export uses RF's live catalogue, and your settings backup does not contain the imported CSV. Keep the original file. Import and category instructions.

Under Music → Song badges, choose songs from your imported catalogue or enter exact RF sequence names manually. Select Moving heads to add a Moving spotlights badge to their song-list cards in Jukebox and Voting. NEW always keeps its corner sash; songs with both selections show the sash and a separate Moving spotlights pill. The combined section shows both selection counts, separate manual name lists and the Show “New this year” filter option. This does not change categories, requests or which lights run. Both choices are available during CSV import and later through Set song badges. Clear badges clears both pending lists, including names outside the CSV. Cancel, X and Escape discard pending badge choices.

Animate moving-head badges adds an optional small spotlight and a faint light wash inside marked song cards. It starts off, works in both templates and music modes, and respects reduced-motion preferences. It is decorative only; it does not control your lights.

The import window keeps its actions visible while you scroll. Set up and turn on category filters from this CSV enables the reviewed filters when you apply; leaving it unchecked keeps your current category settings.

The sample catalogue demonstrates a Moving spotlights badge, a badge alongside NEW, and one animated spotlight badge. These illustrative examples do not change your saved song choices or animation setting; imported songs use your own settings.

Switching themes and reusing details

The first time you start a theme, a compact review groups the settings you have changed from the source theme’s defaults. Changed names, logos, navigation preferences, FAQs, guidance and messages start selected. Open Review to choose individual settings or messages. Cleared text and removed list entries count as changes; lists are reused as a whole. Unchanged values use the new theme’s defaults. If nothing has been customised, the new theme opens directly.

Dates & song selections and Custom colours start unchecked. You can optionally reuse an imported song catalogue with its category and badge choices, or keep the new theme’s palette and seasonal details. Start fresh uses all new-theme defaults. Cancel changes nothing, and the source design stays intact.

After creation, Reuse more from Christmas (or your source theme) makes it easy to bring across a skipped detail. Reuse details from another saved design…, under Theme & style and Change template, remains available later. This uses designs saved in this browser, not an existing RF viewer page. Later reuse starts unchecked and compares current and incoming values before replacing anything; already matching values are omitted. Applying choices supports Undo/Redo, including an optionally copied catalogue.

Returning to a saved theme restores it immediately. When previously copied practical details change, such as an FM frequency, reused name or custom logo link, a quiet notice offers Review changes or Keep saved details. Review shows both values; fields edited on both sides start unchecked. Updates are never applied automatically. Keeping saved values stays quiet until those source details change again. Reviewing a new logo link does not re-enable a logo you have deliberately hidden.

5. Keep a settings backup

The customiser saves your edits locally in this browser. Use Back up saved themes in either template to keep a portable copy of that template’s saved designs, and Load settings backup to continue later or on another computer. Loading first lists the themes it will replace, with a chance to download your current settings. Themes absent from the backup are retained. Cancel, the X and Escape leave your work unchanged. Clearing browser data can remove local edits. To move from a local preview or another website address, download a settings backup there and load it here. Import your song CSV separately.

6. Copy your page into RF

Choose Finish & export above the settings. It takes you to any fields needing attention, or to Copy HTML and Download my HTML. If Copy/Download HTML are disabled, the explanation and links to the fields needing attention appear beside those buttons. Downloaded HTML is named after your show and theme. In RF, create a separate draft under Viewer Page → New Page, replace its HTML with the complete document, then save and check RF's validator and preview. Test your own show before choosing Set as Live.

After copying, a highlighted Copied! confirmation shows that your complete page is on the clipboard. Copy again repeats the same document; if clipboard access fails, select the displayed HTML or download it instead.

On older browsers without CSS :has() support, the viewer presents one scrollable page with section links and no category/NEW filters. Current browsers retain the normal page tabs and filters. This fallback does not add JavaScript or change RF’s request rules.

Both music modes and availability states are included in the export. No custom JavaScript enters your RF page. Real requests, voting, availability, countdown values and playback are supplied by Remote Falcon.

Prefer to edit the HTML yourself?

Choose the Lights on Sunset package or Compact console package, unzip it, and open START-HERE.html. Each includes that layout’s Christmas, Halloween, Thanksgiving, Australia Day, US Patriotic and Valentine’s Day HTML starters, fonts, instructions, credits and licences. Both packages include the new seasonal WebP artwork and lightweight SVG accents; Lights on Sunset also includes its optional Christmas/Halloween WebP illustrations. You do not need to use the customiser.

The guide covers NEW sashes, Announcements, support cards, image hosting and other optional features.

The package also includes README.html: an offline, browser-readable copy of this quick start with its screenshots included in the file.

US Patriotic and Valentine’s Day

US Patriotic brings stars, stripes and Fourth of July celebrations to both layouts. Eagle artwork, accurate SVG American flags and striped ribbons frame the header. White player and queue panels stand apart from navy song cards, with blue information cards and red support cards. Rounded headings complete the theme; Lights on Sunset uses an eagle for Home.

Valentine’s Day pairs roses and flowing ribbon with a heart-shaped chocolate box and love letter. Cream player panels sit above deep rose song choices, with chocolate and blush details and Elegant headings. Lights on Sunset uses Cupid for Home. Both themes retain the familiar Music, Info and Support icons, and custom choices still take priority.

Both themes keep all existing settings. Choose the top image under Site setup → Header, logo & show name → Header artwork. Lower artwork, navbar details and gentle motion stay under Theme & style → Seasonal decorations. US Patriotic sways the header flags and alternates small fireworks that rise, burst and fade in the upper corners. Fireworks follow the animation switch even when you change or hide the header artwork. Valentine’s has a fuller flow of gently rising hearts. Decorations never intercept taps. Reduced-motion preferences stop decorative movement and hide the fireworks and drifting hearts. Personal colours, logos, wording and icon choices retain priority. Both templates include three pictures per theme, usable as header artwork or a logo. Neither theme adds an automatic countdown.

Both templates save each theme separately. Older backups update only the designs they contain, preserving other saved themes. To install a new theme, export fresh HTML and replace the intended RF viewer page; changing the customiser does not update an installed page.

Thanksgiving and Australia Day

Under Site setup → Theme & style, Thanksgiving pairs amber lights and autumn leaves with a friendly turkey, pumpkin pie and cranberries. Cream player, queue and listening cards, forest-green information cards and cranberry support cards add variety to its warm brown song choices. Its welcoming starter wording and colours remain editable. Australia Day pairs flag blue and white with true green cards, gold trim, flag bunting and illustrated BBQ, cricket and beach details. Its Now playing, Up next and request queue use flag blue, distinct from the green song choices. Compact console includes a matching colour preset with advanced colour options. Personal card, accent and text colours take priority over these starter surfaces.

Choose Header artwork under Header, logo & show name, and Images in lower corners under Seasonal decorations, independently: show either, both or neither. Hidden artwork leaves no reserved space. Show navbar details stays separate. Thanksgiving’s Show falling leaves adds a light shower across the full screen, independent of the header artwork; leaves never block taps and are hidden for reduced motion. Australia Day’s Allow gentle animation sways its theme-default top bunting; there are no falling flags. Lights on Sunset uses a turkey Home icon for Thanksgiving and a Southern Cross for Australia Day, with custom icons still available. Compact console keeps its Music, Info and Support icons. Motion respects reduced-motion preferences. The centre of the header remains available for your name or logo. These themes have no countdown; Christmas/Halloween countdown settings are retained when switching back.

Older two-theme Compact backups still load. Loading one replaces only its Christmas/Halloween designs, leaving any newer themed designs intact.

Help and feedback

Choose Help → Feedback & questions for short forms to report a problem, share feedback, suggest an improvement or ask a question. A free GitHub account is needed. Read the setup guide first, then use GitHub Issues for bugs and suggestions. Share generic examples rather than private settings or catalogues. Report security issues privately.

Have a viewer page you love? Share it for consideration as a community template. Include the HTML code, original author and licence or permission to reuse it. Only submit pages you have permission to share and adapt, not purchased templates. Remove private information before posting; issues and attachments are public. Submissions are reviewed for suitability and RF compatibility, and inclusion is not guaranteed.

Prefer to discuss your viewer page privately? Message christmasdave on AusChristmasLighting. The same permission requirements apply.
